macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street climbs as Nasdaq reaches record high
items.summary: U.S. stocks rose Monday, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.7%, the Dow 0.2% and the Nasdaq 1.1% to a record close. Nvidia and Broadcom each advanced 2.1%, supporting technology shares.

items.title: Asian shares advance as oil prices ease
items.summary: Asian equities mostly gained Tuesday after Wall Street’s advance; Japan’s Nikkei rose 1.1% above 70,000. Brent crude fell 0.8% to about $99.48 per barrel as supply concerns eased.

items.title: Treasury yields remain near multiyear highs
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield held around 5.30% after briefly exceeding 5.35%, its highest level since 2002, amid inflation concerns, energy-price pressures and rising government debt.

items.title: Markets await Federal Reserve meeting minutes
items.summary: Investors are looking to the Federal Reserve’s September meeting minutes for clues on whether policymakers favor another rate change. Weaker employment data has reduced expectations for an October rate hike, with markets increasingly pricing a hold.

items.title: Schneider Electric agrees to acquire PTC
items.summary: Schneider Electric agreed to buy industrial-software company PTC for $205 per share in cash, valuing PTC’s equity at approximately $22.6 billion and representing a 42.3% premium to its prior closing price.

items.title: Morgan Stanley turns more constructive on the U.S. dollar
items.summary: Morgan Stanley shifted its currency outlook to neutral with a bullish bias, citing a weaker U.S. payrolls report and reduced expectations for an October Federal Reserve rate hike.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $85,600 as crypto market rally loses momentum
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $85,630, down approximately 0.6% over 24 hours, while Solana and XRP remained near $120.04 and $1.51, respectively.[1]

items.title: CFTC opens consultation on national retail crypto framework
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission launched consultation on a federal framework for retail crypto commodity transactions, including proposed rules on intermediaries, customer-asset segregation and reserves.[2]

items.title: FinCEN withdraws proposed unhosted-wallet and mixer rules
items.summary: FinCEN withdrew two proposed measures targeting transfers involving self-hosted wallets and crypto-mixing services, citing public feedback and reducing previously proposed reporting obligations for self-custody users.[1]

items.title: Ethereum developers test Glamsterdam upgrade on Sepolia
items.summary: Ethereum core developers began testing the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Sepolia test network, rehearsing proposed changes involving account abstraction and data-availability improvements.[1]

items.title: Solana launches open-source institutional delivery-versus-payment system
items.summary: An open-source Solana program designed to settle institutional trades atomically within seconds was reportedly released, with development input from JPMorgan.[3]

items.title: Polymarket unveils Protocol V2
items.summary: Polymarket introduced a redesigned smart-contract protocol for prediction markets and plans to migrate new markets to Protocol V2 beginning November 2.[3]

items.title: Payward expands 24/7 institutional dollar payments in Singapore
items.summary: Payward connected its payment network with Singapore Gulf Bank to provide round-the-clock U.S.-dollar settlement for some institutional customers in selected jurisdictions.[3]

items.title: BNB Chain overtakes Tron in stablecoin-holder count
items.summary: BNB Chain reportedly surpassed Tron to become the blockchain with the largest number of stablecoin holders, while Solana recorded high network activity despite subdued SOL price performance.[4]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Reflection AI unveils Beam open-weight model
items.summary: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI announced Beam, a 501-billion-parameter sparse model with 23 billion active parameters, targeting coding, reasoning, scientific and agentic workloads. The company says it can match leading Chinese models with substantially lower compute requirements; Apache 2.0 weights are expected later this month.

items.title: GitHub releases ReviewBench for AI code-review agents
items.summary: GitHub launched a public research preview of ReviewBench, an open benchmark and leaderboard intended to evaluate the performance of AI agents that review software code.

items.title: SAS launches AI Navigator governance platform
items.summary: SAS introduced AI Navigator, a standalone SaaS product for inventorying and governing models, agents and enterprise AI use cases. The service is available through Microsoft Marketplace.

items.title: Ai2 releases cited scientific-report model
items.summary: The Allen Institute for AI released an open-weights 8-billion-parameter model designed to generate scientific reports with citations and added it as a Fast mode in its Asta system.

items.title: Nvidia and partners introduce Open Agent Safety Platform
items.summary: Nvidia announced an Open Agent Safety Platform with more than 100 participating companies, including Anthropic, Microsoft and Salesforce, aimed at helping organizations monitor and constrain autonomous AI agents.

items.title: Cognition introduces overnight memory for Devin
items.summary: Cognition launched Devin “Dreaming,” a feature that organizes and links an agent’s memory graph overnight. The company is also open-sourcing a Git- and Markdown-backed agent-memory format.

items.title: Strands Labs releases open decision model for agents
items.summary: AWS-affiliated Strands Labs released an open 2-billion-parameter model designed to select among supplied options in agent workflows, targeting lightweight decision-making rather than general-purpose generation.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Steam reportedly reaches record $1.7 billion in September revenue
items.summary: An estimate from Alinea Analytics says Steam generated about $1.7 billion in September 2026, up 13% year over year and driven heavily by free-to-play games. Wardogs was reportedly the month’s top new release by Steam revenue, followed by Onimusha: Way of the Sword and The Blood of Dawnwalker.

items.title: Supermassive Games reportedly cuts more than 70 jobs
items.summary: Supermassive Games is reportedly consulting on more than 70 layoffs following the release of Directive 8020. The cuts are part of broader reported layoffs and financial pressure across the UK and North American games industry.

items.title: Take-Two signs long-term Xbox publishing agreement
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive reportedly renewed or expanded its publishing agreement with Xbox, covering all Xbox devices. The deal comes ahead of the expected November 2026 release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

items.title: Roblox adds agentic AI tools for game creation
items.summary: Roblox is reportedly introducing AI features that can help developers plan, build, and test games on its platform. The tools are intended to automate parts of the game-development workflow.

items.title: Esports remains part of Asian Games program after 2026
items.summary: The Olympic Council of Asia reportedly denied claims that esports would leave the Asian Games after 2026. It said a new Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games would be held in Kuwait, while esports continued to feature in regional competition.
